page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-standard-8-lssd is a network-optimized virtual machine instance configured with 8 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs and 30 GB of system memory, providing 3.75 GB of RAM per core. The instance integrates local storage comprising a 403 GB NVMe solid-state drive, eliminating the need to provision standalone block volumes for temporary disk access. It operates without discrete GPU accelerators and does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The hardware configuration pairs dedicated core scheduling with direct-attached NVMe storage. By provisioning the 403 GB NVMe SSD directly to the node, the architecture delivers high local disk throughput and minimal I/O latency. A primary tradeoff involves the ephemeral nature of direct-attached NVMe media, which requires users to maintain state redundancy elsewhere, alongside the 3.75 GB per core ratio that aligns closely with standard rather than memory-heavy profiles.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the integrated NVMe storage optimizes spending by eliminating external storage provisioning overhead for high-IOPS scratch disks and transient caches. Google Cloud Platform c4n-standard-8-lssd is well suited for database replicas, distributed caching tiers, search index workers, continuous integration nodes, and low-latency transactional processing environments.
